user: A separate general question: what is a SEPA transfer?
answer:
What I did
- Checked Verta documentation on transfers and tariffs.

What I found
- A SEPA transfer is a payment sent to banks within the Single Euro Payments Area (euro‑area banks) and reaches the beneficiary bank within one business day.
- Fee components (from the tariff): flat fee EUR 0.35 and percentage fee 0.0% (the percentage fee is calculated on the EUR equivalent, if applicable).
- Note: SEPA outgoing transfers count toward your settled outgoing transfer limits once they are settled.

What happens next
- If you want to make a SEPA transfer, I can help start it or show the exact fee for a specific amount. Would you like me to do that?

fragments.text:
Transfers
## Transfer types
Internal transfers move funds between Verta accounts and settle instantly.
SEPA transfers reach euro-area banks within one business day. SWIFT transfers
are used for other destinations and settle in one to five business days. Card
payments are outgoing payments to a merchant.

Verta tariff schedule
## Transfer fees by type
| Transfer type | Flat fee | Percentage fee |
|---|---|---|
| Internal | EUR 0.00 | 0% |
| SEPA | EUR 0.35 | 0% |
| SWIFT | EUR 15.00 | 0.3% |
| Card payment | EUR 0.00 | 1.2% |

The percentage fee is calculated on the EUR equivalent of the transfer amount.

Verta tariff schedule
## Account tiers
Verta offers three account tiers: Tier 1, Tier 2 and Tier 3. The tier of
each account sets its pricing as well as its daily and per-month transfer
limits.

Limit operations
## What counts towards a limit
Only settled outgoing transfers count towards the daily and monthly transfer
limits. Card payments count. Incoming transfers, internal transfers between the
own accounts of one customer, and fees charged by Verta do not count.
